title: MERT wins the coarse question and loses the fine one, and the fine one is the only one left
question: Should a learned music embedding replace the hand built descriptor?

model.name: m-a-p/MERT-v1-95M
model.size: 95M parameters, 12 layers, 768 dimensions, 24 kHz, 5 s context
model.loads_without_remote_code: The published config names custom modules, but the weights load into a plain transformers HubertModel with zero missing, unexpected or mismatched keys.
model.throughput: 8.7 files per second on the Apple GPU
model.licence: cc-by-nc-4.0, which would have needed answering before any music made with it was sold
model.cost_if_adopted: torch, transformers, a sidecar environment on a different Python, and about 400 MB of weights, against a project whose dependency count is zero

two_tasks.coarse: Which family is this: bass, pad, drum kit, guitar. Leave one out over the library, 900 probes.
two_tasks.fine: Which preset inside a known family made this sound. Sixty presets rendered in Live, each ranked against its own family only, exact ground truth.

coarse_family_retrieval.verdict: MERT wins by about nine points

fine_within_family_retrieval.verdict: the hand built descriptor wins on every measure, by roughly two to one

result: The two results do not contradict each other. MERT is trained to represent music, which is what a coarse family is, and the abstraction that buys it discards the fine spectral detail that separates one bass from another.
The family is supplied by the caller, because a stem being rebuilt is already named. The coarse question MERT wins is therefore not asked, and the fine question it loses is the whole task.
The pure Python descriptor stays, and now stays because it measured better rather than because it was already there.
scope_and_weakness: Sixty renders, about five per family, and the per family figures cannot carry a percentage.

The renders are dry and the previews are produced, so both descriptors are being asked to cross a domain gap. That the gap is the same for both is what makes the comparison fair; it is not a measurement of either one at its best.
Time averaged hidden states, one layer at a time. A pooled or concatenated representation, or a layer combination, was not tried, and neither was the 330M model.
MERT was given no fine tuning of any kind. A model trained on this library's own previews is a different and untested proposition.
recorded_also_in_note: This record is the only published account of the measurement. What it also went into at the time were working notes kept outside the repository.
